title: United States and Iceland hold annual bilateral Strategic Dialogue
excerpt: Officials from both nations met in Reykjavik to discuss security cooperation and regional domain awareness.
bodyHtml:
The United States and Iceland held the annual bilateral Strategic Dialogue in Reykjavik from November 2-3, according to the US State Department.

The meeting was led by U.S. Department of State Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs Deputy Assistant Secretary Peter Andreoli, Office of the Secretary of War Principal Director for Europe and NATO Policy Alton Buland, Icelandic Director General for International Affairs and Policy Anna Hjartardóttir, and Director General for Defense Jónas Allansson.

Participants also included U.S. Ambassador to Iceland Billy Long and Icelandic Ambassador to the United States Svanhildur Hólm Valsdóttir. The United States and Iceland marked 75 years of close bilateral defense and security cooperation.

Discussions addressed the evolving European security landscape and wider global security challenges, with particular emphasis on enhancing cooperation in the Arctic, reinforcing NATO’s collective deterrence and defense, and advancing bilateral security initiatives. The Dialogue also focused on improving regional domain awareness, protection of critical infrastructure, and countering malign influence and subversive activities. Participants explored new opportunities for dual-use technologies, supply chain security, innovation, and collaboration with the U.S. National Guard.
